t: Tags, data types and I/O addresses
html:
A tag is a named piece of controller memory with a type. Logix Connect uses the Logix types you will meet in Studio 5000:

TypeWhat it holdsWhere you use it
BOOLone bit, 0 or 1every input and output, every latch, every one-shot storage bit
SINT / INT / DINT / LINTan 8, 16, 32 or 64-bit integer (and the unsigned USINT, UINT, UDINT)counts, analog values (INT from the modules), shift registers (DINT, one bit per stop)
REAL / LREALa floating-point numberscaled analog values, calculations
STRINGup to 82 characters, members .LEN and .DATAmessages to and from a socket or a code reader
TIMER.PRE (preset, ms), .ACC (accumulated, ms), .EN, .TT (timing), .DN (done)TON / TOF / RTO
COUNTER.PRE, .ACC, .CU, .CD, .DN, .OV, .UNCTU / CTD
CONTROL.LEN, .POS, .EN, .EU, .DN, .EM, .ER, .UL, .IN, .FDBSL / BSR / FFL / FFU / SQO / SQI
arraysExist[0..1]: a DINT with Dim 2a 64-bit shift register, addressed Exist[0].12 for bit 12

Integers wrap at the limits of their type the way the controller does (an INT at 32767 plus 1 is −32768), and a REAL rounds to 32-bit float. Open Controller Tags → Edit Tags. Type a name in the * row at the bottom and press Enter; pick the type; add a description. A description is free and is shown in the ladder when View → Tag Descriptions in Ladder is on; the lessons rely on them. A tag’s Style (Decimal, Binary, Octal, Hex, ASCII; Float and Exponential for a REAL) is only how it is displayed; the shift registers in Part IV are Binary so you can watch the bits walk. Right-click a tag for Tag Properties…: name, description, base or alias, data type and Dim, style and scope.

Base tags: the I/O points

The chassis points exist as tags already: Local:1:I.Data.0, Local:4:O.Data.3, Local:7:I.Ch1Data. You can write them straight into a rung, and the I/O Monitor shows them live, but a program full of slot numbers is unreadable. That is what aliases are for.

Alias tags

An alias is a tag that is another tag under a better name: Start_PB aliased to Local:3:I.Data.1. Reading or writing the alias reads or writes the point. In the tag editor, choose Alias and pick the base in Alias For.

Logix Connect has a house rule that saves most of that work: a tag named Device_Signal aliases itself. Place a light called Lamp_Run; its signal is On; create a tag called Lamp_Run_On (or type the name into a rung) and it is aliased to the light’s point automatically. Each part’s Properties drawer lists its signals with their points and the alias each one has; its Alias tags button does that part, and Alias all I/O (the properties panel with nothing selected) or Tools → Create Alias Tags for Wired I/O does every signal on the floor at once. Pressing it again creates nothing, because one alias per point is enough.

Under every signal in the drawer there is also a tag box. Pick a tag there and that signal uses the tag itself, with no I/O point and no alias: a button or sensor writes the tag, and a light or actuator follows it. That is the quick way; wiring to a point and aliasing it is how a real machine is done, so the book uses points. Do not give a button a tag that your ladder also writes with an OTE, or the two will fight.

Part IV uses shorter, LogixPro-style names for the bottle line (LS1, Cap_Ram, Supply_Inlet), made as explicit aliases; the full list is in Appendix A. Either style is fine; the rule is that a rung should read like the machine, not like the chassis.

Controller tags and program tags

Controller tags belong to the whole controller: every program and routine can use them, and all I/O and alias tags live here. Program tags (Parameters and Local Tags under a program in the organizer) belong to one program, and only that program’s routines can see them. Two programs can each have their own Step without touching each other; inside a program its own tag wins, as in Logix. Every program in this book keeps its tags at controller scope, so they show in one list.

Bits of a word

Any integer tag can be used a bit at a time: Exist[0].12 is bit 12 of the first DINT of the array Exist. In Monitor Tags a DINT has a + that lists its 32 bits, each toggleable, with the bits the program uses shaded; the ▾ beside any integer opens the Studio 5000 bit grid. The Data Table (under Watch and Cross Reference in the organizer, or Window → Open Data Table) shows whole words in the radix of your choice, the way RSLogix’s data files did.

Watch for

Names: letters, digits and single underscores, starting with a letter, up to 40 characters, no trailing underscore, and no two tags the same ignoring case. Run and run are the same tag. An instruction mnemonic (TON, ADD) cannot be a tag name.
